text: We can move the deletion of existing Pods to a dedicated controller (or even to ). However, workload controllers still must obey the rule: when has , stop Pod creation and wait until is gone. If the controller that creates Pods does not pause while victim Pods terminate, it immediately creates replacement Pods. Then the controller and the workload controller fight each other in a loop (one creates Pods while the other deletes them). This loop also keeps the finalizer on and blocks deletion. A dedicated controller reduces the responsibility of workload controllers, but it does not remove the fragile contract around pausing Pod creation and controller delegation.

text: Thanks for looking! Nobody starts the interactive REPL on purpose with stdin set to NUL. The trouble is that tools which run commands non-interactively hand the process NUL as stdin, and since NUL is a character device, reports True. So an accidental bare , or with an empty heredoc, lands in pyrepl instead of reading EOF and exiting. Where I hit it: AI coding agents. Claude Code's shell tool on Windows runs every command with stdin = NUL and output captured, so anyone using it on Windows can hit this. The process never returns: it spins writing tracebacks (about 4 MB in 3 seconds here) until the tool's timeout kills it. hyperfine also defaults stdin to NUL (that's how #133430 got there), and CI runners and schedulers commonly do the same. The basic REPL ( ) reads EOF and exits at once, which is what these tools need. A possible check: fails on NUL even though succeeds: So pyrepl could fall back to the basic REPL when fails on stdin, or at least stop retrying after the first from .

text: **Update / root cause on my side (follow-up to my earlier comments):** In my case this turned out **not** to be a bug in the integration or in – the entity had been **disabled in the entity registry**. A disabled entity is never added to hass, so it never subscribes to the dispatcher signal and therefore never fires . After re-enabling the entity and restarting Home Assistant, everything works again on 2026.10.1. To verify, I ran a copy of the core integration (unchanged apart from added log lines) as a custom component and traced the full path. Before the fix: …and nothing else – no entity was listening. After re-enabling the entity: **Important for others landing here:** the debug line is **not** the cause of missing events. The integration uses the library's raw ERP1 callback ( ), which is emitted *before* EEP decoding. text: The changelog entry you linked, dated April 1, 2026, states that some older cooling appliance models no longer support the refrigerator camera features and that the /images endpoint has become unavailable for those models. It does not announce a deprecation or shutdown of the Images API itself. The only other images-related entry, from September 2025, concerns a fix for missing image permission scopes in newly created apps, which suggests that the API remains a supported feature. Regarding how this affects your PR: Appliances that no longer support the feature will return an error when the Images API is called. The coordinator already handles this during the initial refresh: it logs the error at debug level and simply creates no camera entities. The delayed refresh after a door closes behaves the same way, so this does not break anything or generate excessive logs. There is one side effect worth noting: for such appliances, every door close still schedules an Images API request 60 seconds later, which then fails. This consumes a few requests per day from the per-appliance quota. Given the debounce, the number of requests is small. The retry is also what allows the cameras to recover when a request fails due to a transient issue, so I would keep the current behavior. If a reviewer raises this concern, a possible future improvement would be to stop scheduling refreshes once the API reports that the feature is unsupported. However, the changelog does not specify which error code these models return, so this would need to be confirmed against a real device.
